articles.chapeau: How to get to Vespucci Island and get yourself a 10-second car
articles.txt:
In GTA 6 , Brian O'Conner's green Mitsubishi Eclipse from the first Fast & Furious movie can be yours if you know where to look. The car is a direct reference to the one we see Paul Walker's character driving early in the movie. It's a pretty fast car that can help you to quickly traverse the map and escape the police. Considering how good this car is, it's surprisingly easy to rob, making it a perfect special car to look for early in the game — as long as you have the funds to keep it for yourself .
Below, you learn where to find Brian's green Mitsubishi Eclipse in GTA 6 .
To get the chance to add Brian's Mitsubishi Eclipse, also known as the '97 Maibatsu Penumbra FF, to your collection, you must go to Vespucci Island in Vice-Dale County . This area is on the east coast , and Vespucci Island is one of three Rialto Islands in the Vice Beach region, northeast of Vice City.
Graphic: Paulo Kawanishi/Polygon | Source images: Rockstar Games Once you reach Vespucci Island, turn left onto the street heading north when coming from the west . Right on the corner, opposite a construction site, you will see a big house with a white gate . As you approach the place, the gate will automatically open. There are no guards around, so don't worry about NPCs spotting you entering the house.
Graphic: Paulo Kawanishi/Polygon | Source images: Rockstar Games Go to the door beside the garage . It's locked, and your only option is to break it, but you must be quick, because as soon as you break the door, the alarm will go off. Inside the garage, you will find the green Mitsubishi Eclipse. Open the garage then get into the car. If you have already met Moses in Chapter 2, you can use the slim jim to open the car without smashing the window.
After you get out of the house, you can pay $6,750 to register it . You can also sell it for $1,100 , but this car is excellent and you should consider keeping it. Here's its stats:

Check out our GTA 6 beginner guide to get a grasp of the basics and our tips for what to do first , recommendations for the best ways to make money fast , and an explainer for how to keep stolen weapons and cars to make the most of your free time.
Our selection of GTA 6 guides includes help for things like how to steal the Phoenix in "Unwanted Attention" and whether you should defuse Mandy , too. There's a set of explainers for GTA 6 's more open-ended side activities, like how to rob the Exotic Animal Front and where to find tree effigies for the Skunk Ape mission , and we've got all the GTA 6 cheat codes . You'll have to put in some effort before you can use those, though.

articles.t: GTA 6 : un joueur prétend avoir été suspendu du PSN pour une photo de nudistes envoyée à un ami
articles.chapeau: Un joueur de GTA 6 affirme avoir perdu la messagerie et les fonctions sociales du PSN pour une photo de nudistes prise dans le jeu. Sony n'a pas commenté.
articles.txt:
Un joueur de GTA 6 affirme avoir perdu pour 30 jours l'accès aux fonctions sociales du PlayStation Network. En cause, selon lui, une photo prise avec l'appareil du jeu dans une colonie nudiste de Leonida, qu'il avait envoyée à un ami par la messagerie de la PS5.
Sous le pseudo DerrickGott007, il a publié sur X le lendemain de la sortie un message tout en majuscules qui supplie les autres joueurs de ne jamais envoyer sur le réseau de Sony de photos du jeu « qui contiennent de la nudité ».
Le message s'accompagne d'une photo de son téléviseur, sur lequel s'affiche la notification de PlayStation Safety. Elle indique qu'un contenu envoyé depuis son compte dans la messagerie PlayStation enfreint le code de conduite, que le compte ne peut plus utiliser les fonctions sociales jusqu'au 20 décembre et que le motif retenu est un « contenu pornographique ou obscène » .
Sony y prévient aussi qu'une récidive pourrait entraîner une suspension temporaire ou définitive de l'ensemble des services PlayStation. La notification ne nomme ni GTA 6 ni l'image en cause, si bien que le lien entre les deux repose sur la seule parole du joueur. Sony n'a pas réagi.
Le jeu de Rockstar est classé PEGI 18 en Europe ; aux États-Unis, l'ESRB liste la nudité et le contenu sexuel explicite parmi ses descripteurs. Les classifications australienne et néo-zélandaise évoquaient le sexe et la nudité dès le début d'octobre, tout comme la fiche PEGI détaillée publiée puis retirée dans la foulée.
Une colonie nudiste au détour de la carte colle parfaitement à la Floride caricaturale que la série moque depuis Vice City. Le jeu peut montrer ces scènes à un adulte qui l'a acheté, alors que la messagerie de Sony relève d'autres règles, qui ne font aucune différence entre une photo réelle et une image du jeu.
Le précédent le plus connu remonte à Watch Dogs 2 , en novembre 2016. Un joueur qui avait partagé la capture d'un personnage nu avait reçu de Sony un avis de suspension pour contenu à caractère sexuel.
La sanction avait été levée peu après, selon ses dires. Ubisoft avait présenté ses excuses avant de modifier le modèle en cause par un patch.
Le code de conduite de la communauté PlayStation demande de ne pas partager, distribuer ni stocker de « contenu obscène, pornographique ou illégal ».
Il couvre tout ce qui transite par les services de Sony, messages compris, ainsi que ce que les joueurs créent ou partagent dans les jeux. Sur sa page d'assistance, le constructeur précise que tout contenu inapproprié téléversé peut être examiné par son équipe de sécurité.
Pour ne pas finir comme DerrickGott007, mieux vaut n'envoyer aucune capture dénudée par la messagerie de la PS5 ou par l'application PlayStation, même pour en rire.
La copie sur une clé USB, depuis la galerie multimédia, permet de récupérer une photo sur son ordinateur sans passer par les serveurs de Sony. Une suspension temporaire ne peut faire l'objet d' aucun appel , Sony réservant sa procédure aux suspensions définitives prononcées au cours des six derniers mois.
La sanction de DerrickGott007 tombe pile au moment où tout le monde compare ses trouvailles de Leonida. Ceux qui commencent tout juste leur partie trouveront dans nos premières choses à faire de quoi s'occuper sans risquer la suspension.

[Vidéo] GTA 6 : "Abrutissant, abêtissant et avilissant" : peut-on se divertir n’importe comment ? - Tribune Chrétienne
articles.chapeau: De Jordan Bardella à Emmanuel Grégoire, GTA 6 dépasse les clivages politiques pour réunir des responsables publics dans un même engouement pour un divertissement où la violence, la vulgarité et la débauche sont omniprésentes. Mais un chrétien peut-il vraiment se divertir avec n’importe quoi ?
articles.txt:
Jordan Bardella et Emmanuel Grégoire ont manifestement découvert une passion commune. L’un préside le Rassemblement national, l’autre dirige la mairie de Paris sous les couleurs socialistes. Tout semble les opposer politiquement, mais il aura suffi de la sortie de GTA 6 pour les réunir dans un même enthousiasme. Il faut reconnaître que l’événement mérite qu’on s’y arrête : voir deux responsables politiques de sensibilités aussi différentes communier dans leur impatience de découvrir un univers de vols, de violences, de trafics et de débauche constitue une forme assez inattendue de réconciliation nationale.
🔴GTA 6 : « Abrutissant, abêtissant et avilissant » : peut-on se divertir n’importe comment ? ➡️ De Jordan Bardella à Emmanuel Grégoire, GTA 6 dépasse les clivages politiques pour réunir des responsables publics dans un même engouement pour un divertissement où la violence, la… pic.twitter.com/tcSktyb20q
Le 16 novembre, invité des Grandes Gueules sur RMC, Jordan Bardella ne dissimulait pas son impatience : « Je l’attends, c’est le jeu d’une génération. » Évoquant les précédents épisodes, Vice City et San Andreas, auxquels il avait joué plus jeune, le président du RN ajoutait : « Évidemment que je l’essaierai, je ne vais pas vous dire le contraire. » Une déclaration accompagnée d’une plaisanterie sur les nombreux arrêts maladie que pourrait provoquer la sortie du jeu. Voilà donc un sujet sur lequel le président du Rassemblement national ne semble éprouver aucune hésitation.
À l’autre extrémité de l’échiquier politique, Emmanuel Grégoire n’était pas davantage insensible à l’événement. Dans la nuit du 18 au 19 novembre, le maire socialiste de Paris publiait sur Instagram une image du téléchargement de GTA 6, accompagnée d’un enthousiaste « Let’s go !!!! » . La publication provoquait une petite polémique lorsque des internautes l’accusaient d’être arrivé en retard au Conseil de Paris après avoir passé la nuit à jouer. L’élu démentait, assurant avoir honoré dès 9 heures un rendez-vous avec le déontologue de la Ville. La déontologie était donc sauve. Quant au discernement culturel, la question reste entière.
Car il faut tout de même s’interroger sur cette fascination pour un divertissement dont l’ambition intellectuelle ne saute pas précisément aux yeux. On peut admirer la prouesse technologique, la richesse graphique et la complexité de l’univers imaginé par Rockstar Games. Mais il serait difficile de soutenir que multiplier les infractions virtuelles, évoluer dans un univers saturé de vulgarité ou se divertir de comportements criminels constitue, en soi, un exercice particulièrement élevé de l’intelligence.
On ne demandera évidemment pas à chaque jeu vidéo de rivaliser avec les Pensées de Pascal ou la Somme théologique de saint Thomas d’Aquin. Le divertissement a ses droits. Mais faut-il pour autant renoncer à toute exigence de qualité morale et intellectuelle dès lors qu’il s’agit de s’amuser ?
C’est précisément la question que pose GTA 6, au-delà de son succès commercial et de l’enthousiasme de quelques responsables politiques. Peut-on véritablement se divertir avec n’importe quoi ?
La réponse de la tradition catholique est particulièrement éclairante. Dans la Somme théologique (IIa-IIae, question 168), saint Thomas d’Aquin reconnaît la nécessité du jeu et du repos de l’esprit. Il développe la notion d’eutrapélie, cette vertu qui permet de se divertir avec mesure et convenance. L’homme ne peut vivre dans un effort intellectuel ou physique permanent. La détente est donc légitime, et même nécessaire.Mais le Docteur angélique précise que les divertissements doivent demeurer conformes à la raison et à la dignité humaine. Leur caractère plaisant ne suffit pas à les rendre moralement bons. Le contenu du jeu, les intentions de celui qui s’y livre et la place qu’il occupe dans son existence doivent être examinés.
Lire aussi : https://tribunechretienne.com/leon-xiv-nous-sommes-tous-egaux-devant-la-loi-de-dieu/

Ils participent directement à l’expérience ludique. La violence, la cupidité et la transgression deviennent des ressorts du plaisir proposé au joueur.

articles.txt:
Miss driving around Los Santos in first person? For presumably immersion reasons, Grand Theft Auto 6 doesn’t have a dedicated first-person mode ( yet ), but a camera glitch lets you see Vice City through Jason or Lucia’s eyes, and it works inside a vehicle and also while you’re running around. All you need is a car, your in-game phone and a bit of timing.
Like I mentioned, it’s actually quite easy to do, it just might be a bit finicky. Check out the video above or follow the simple instructions below:
It’s usually just a case of repeating this method over and over until it works.
The view sticks when you get out of the car, so you can walk around and shoot in first person as well as drive. Some menus that move the camera, like browsing at a vendor, can end the glitch. We’re not sure how buying stuff would work in this view anyway.
Quite an easy fix if you’re getting bored of first-person. Just save and reload your game to get your usual camera back.
You can also change the touchpad or View button back to Map in the controller settings, and that will undo the first-person glitch.
With almost total certainty, you will not get banned or anything of the sort for performing this first-person glitch. You’re not getting a competitive advantage as this is an offline single-player game.
The framework is there for first-person, so Rockstar seems to have already developed the first-person view with the intention of making it into the game. Whether the first-person view comes to GTA 6 in a future update, its PC port, or even the PS6 release is anyone’s guess. We would expect this glitch to be patched out with the first big update, though.
But you don’t need any guesswork if you’re trying to get into Mile Zero Air Station all sneaky-like.
Grand Theft Auto 6 is available now on PS5 and Xbox Series X and S.

articles.t: GTA à Marseille, Quimper et Sète : la sortie de GTA 6 inspire des parodies très françaises
articles.chapeau: À Marseille, Quimper ou Sète, des passionnés ont recréé GTA dans leur ville grâce à l'IA, à l'occasion de la sortie de GTA 6.
articles.txt:
La sortie de GTA 6 inspire bien au-delà des consoles. À Marseille, Quimper ou Sète, des passionnés ont profité de l’événement pour imaginer leur propre version du jeu dans leur ville, avec l’aide de l’intelligence artificielle. Tour d’horizon de ces parodies très locales.
Pendant que les joueurs du monde entier découvrent Leonida et Vice City , certains Français ont préféré rester chez eux, ou plutôt ramener GTA chez eux. En quelques jours, plusieurs projets amateurs ont fleuri dans la presse régionale, avec un point commun : des créateurs sans studio, qui se sont appuyés sur l’IA pour bâtir en quelques heures ou quelques jours ce qui aurait demandé des mois de travail il y a encore peu.
Le projet le plus ambitieux vient de Marseille. Anis Ayari, ingénieur spécialisé en intelligence artificielle et créateur de contenus suivi par plus de 300 000 abonnés sous le nom de Defend Intelligence , s’est donné treize jours pour réaliser « un GTA à Marseille » , un vieux rêve d’enfant, raconte France 3 Provence-Alpes-Côte d’Azur . Dans une vidéo publiée le 16 novembre, il dévoile une cité phocéenne reconnaissable au premier coup d’œil, avec le Vieux-Port, Notre-Dame-de-la-Garde, la cathédrale de la Major, le château d’If ou encore les lignes de métro et de tramway de la RTM. Le rappeur Jul y fait même une apparition, à bord d’un ovni.
Pour reconstituer la ville, l’ingénieur s’est appuyé sur des données ouvertes, comme la cartographie d’OpenStreetMap, les photos géolocalisées de Panoramax et des relevés LiDAR pour la hauteur des bâtiments. Il a ensuite demandé à l’IA de reconstruire certains monuments « pierre par pierre » à partir de photographies. Le projet rassemble environ 5 000 modèles 3D et a atteint près d’un téraoctet sur son ordinateur, soit environ cinq fois la taille de GTA 6. « Cela m’aurait coûté des milliers d’euros de faire modéliser ça par quelqu’un » , explique-t-il. Son jeu n’est toutefois pas jouable pour l’instant.
En Bretagne, l’ambiance est plus bon enfant. Claire Le Gall, ancienne vétérinaire quimpéroise reconvertie dans le développement, a créé Grand Theft Kemper , une parodie jouable gratuitement en ligne, rapporte Ouest-France . Pas d’armes ici, mais une dizaine de missions qui consistent à retrouver un biniou égaré, récupérer des macarons volés par des goélands ou livrer des crêpes à vélo. On y retrouve pourtant les codes de GTA, de la minicarte aux voitures « empruntées », avec Breizh FM à la radio. Il lui a fallu près de dix-sept heures et 18 000 lignes de code pour reproduire plus de 200 rues de Quimper, du quartier de Locmaria à la gare, parsemées de 83 drapeaux bretons. « Avec l’IA, la seule limite, c’est notre imagination » , estime-t-elle.
Même idée, autre spécialité locale à Sète. Benoît Lebreau a imaginé Grand Tielle Auto Sète , un jeu dans lequel il faut livrer les tielles les plus chaudes le plus vite possible à travers la ville, relate France 3 Occitanie . Sorti le 16 novembre, il aurait déjà attiré plus de 7 000 joueurs. Son créateur y a consacré entre 20 et 30 heures, en s’appuyant sur une IA spécialisée dans le code, sur des modèles 3D réalisés avec des artistes et sur les données d’OpenStreetMap et de l’IGN. Le choix de la ville doit beaucoup au jeu de mots : « Il n’y a pas de ville qui s’appelle six, Troie je ne connais pas assez, il ne restait que Sète » , s’amuse-t-il.
Les créateurs marseillais et sétois se gardent toutefois de survendre l’outil. Anis Ayari reconnaît que son jeu n’est « pas parfait » , entre bugs de circulation, textures qui se chargent progressivement et décors pas toujours fidèles à la réalité. Benoît Lebreau est encore plus clair : « Faire croire qu’un jeu de ce niveau est possible en deux phrases et que l’IA va tout faire facilement, non. Il y a beaucoup d’interprétations de l’IA, qui peut inventer des choses et des graphismes. Il faut constamment reprendre le script et apporter des corrections. »

How Long Is Chapter 2 in GTA 6? All Missables and Mission List
articles.chapeau: Find out how long Chapter 2 is in GTA 6, see the full mission list, and learn what you can miss before leaving Port Gellhorn.
articles.txt:
X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Share using Native tools Share Copied to clipboard Add Us On Google Chapter 2 of Grand Theft Auto VI gives Jason and Lucia a place to lay low in Port Gellhorn, but their stay at the Starlet Motel has an expiration date. Here’s how long the chapter takes, the full mission list, and all the GTA 6 Chapter 2 missables to look out for before you start Checking Out.
“ Checking Out” is the final mission in Chapter 2 of GTA 6 , and starting it permanently removes the Starlet Motel as your safehouse. The mission appears on your map as Move to Vice City once you’ve finished the other main objectives, including Afternoon Delight, and reached the $15,000 goal for Prepare for Vice City. The marker takes you back to your room at the Starlet Motel.
I’d make a manual save in a separate slot before starting the mission. Grand Theft Auto VI doesn’t have mission replay, so keeping that save gives you a way to go back if you realize you forgot something at the motel.
The Starlet Motel is where I’d spend my last few minutes in Chapter 2. You’ll lose access to your room as a home base, so grab the motel collectibles while they’re close by and check the parking lot for Wyman. Some of these collectibles can be found elsewhere in Leonida.
Here is everything you should do before moving on to GTA 6 Chapter 3:
Yes, you can return to Port Gellhorn after Chapter 2. You also keep your cash, bank balance, and cars when you move to Vice City. Billy’s missions continue in Chapter 3, and you can still bring cars to Moses later.
If you’re trying to hit the $15,000 goal before moving out, this is a good time to use the Port Gellhorn safe codes at the Brooks Boatworks, La Cascara Motel, and Kingpin Bowling Illegal Operations in the area.
Chapter 2 of GTA 6 can take around five hours if you purely focus on getting to Vice City. However, give yourself more time if you want to explore Port Gellhorn, do jobs for Billy or Moses, or still need to build up your savings before Checking Out.
In my GTA 6 review playthrough , it took me around 8 hours to complete the chapter. But I also explored the entire map and tackled some secret side quests that I stumbled upon while driving around Port Gellhorn.
Chapter 2 of GTA 6 has 27 missions and tasks if you include optional jobs and smaller objectives , using the same broad count as our Chapter 1 guide . That includes everything from taking care of Jason at the motel to checking out McKittrick Farm.
Here are all 27 Chapter 2 missions and tasks in GTA 6 , from Jason and Lucia’s arrival at the Starlet Motel to their move to Vice City. Some objectives can appear in a different order depending on which jobs you do first.
Once you’ve finished the main missions and saved up $15,000, you’re ready to head to Vice City. Before you start Checking Out, I’d take one last look around the Starlet Motel for any cards or magazines you missed.
However it’s important to reiterate that you can still come back to Port Gellhorn later, but your room at the motel won’t be yours anymore.

articles.t: GTA 6 devient le jeu le plus suivi de l'histoire de Twitch, devant League of Legends
articles.chapeau: Pour sa sortie, GTA 6 a réuni plus de spectateurs simultanés sur Twitch qu'aucun autre jeu avant lui, finale des Worlds de League of Legends comprise.
articles.txt:
D'après les relevés de Streams Charts, le jeu de Rockstar a culminé à 3,31 millions de spectateurs simultanés sur Twitch pour sa sortie.
Le précédent record tenait depuis la finale des Worlds 2022 de League of Legends, entre T1 et DRX, avec 3,11 millions de spectateurs. Fortnite suit, à 3,04 millions en décembre 2023.
Toutes plateformes confondues, la sortie de GTA 6 a réuni jusqu'à 7,9 millions de spectateurs au même moment, dont 3,2 millions sur YouTube et 1,5 million sur Kick. C'est plus de quatre fois le précédent record de lancement, celui de la bêta fermée de Valorant en 2020, avec 1,74 million.
Twitch a aussi compté 36 millions d'heures de visionnage en une seule journée sur GTA 6, un record pour un jeu. Sur Kick, 1 798 chaînes diffusaient le jeu en même temps, deux fois l'ancien record de Fortnite.
Ces chiffres restent provisoires. La Velada del Año, le gala de boxe entre streamers d'Ibai, garde le record absolu de Twitch toutes catégories confondues, avec 9,68 millions de spectateurs simultanés en 2025.
Les joueurs suivent le même mouvement : le jour de la sortie, 61 % des joueurs PS5 actifs aux États-Unis et 56 % des joueurs Xbox actifs dans le monde ont lancé GTA 6. Pour vous y mettre à votre tour, voici nos 10 astuces pour bien débuter .

articles.t: Aliens GTA 6 : où trouver l'OVNI et terminer la quête secrète ?
articles.chapeau: Les mystères extraterrestres ont toujours occupé une place particulière dans l’univers de Grand Theft Auto. Après les nombreux OVNI et [...]
articles.txt:
Les mystères extraterrestres ont toujours occupé une place particulière dans l’univers de Grand Theft Auto. Après les nombreux OVNI et secrets de GTA V, Rockstar Games va encore plus loin dans GTA VI avec une véritable quête secondaire consacrée aux aliens. Cette aventure façon X-Files se déroule en trois étapes. Voici comment trouver les extraterrestres dans GTA 6, résoudre les énigmes et obtenir les récompenses. Notamment des bonus de statistiques permanents.
Déblocage : dès le chapitre 2 Conditions : seul, de nuit, après minuit Étapes : enlèvement par l’OVNI, rêve des extraterrestres, laboratoire secret Lieux : Kelly County pour l’OVNI, sud de Hamlet (Mariana County) pour le laboratoire Récompenses : trophée « La vérité est ailleurs » et bonus permanents de santé, d’endurance et de Concentration Sommaire
Où trouver le premier OVNI et se faire enlever par les aliens dans GTA 6 ? La première rencontre avec les extraterrestres est accessible dès le chapitre 2. Pour déclencher cet événement, rendez-vous dans Kelly County, au nord-ouest de la Prison d’Etat de Leonida ou au sud-est de Port Gellhorn. Vous devez impérativement vous y rendre seul, et de nuit (après minuit), pour avoir une chance de déclencher la rencontre. Sur le bord de la route, cherchez une voiture abandonnée dont les feux clignotent.
Attention, cet événement n’apparaît pas systématiquement. Si la voiture n’est pas présente, éloignez-vous de la zone avant de revenir une autre nuit. Une fois le véhicule repéré, descendez de votre voiture et suivez le petit chemin qui s’enfonce dans les bois. Vous finirez par apercevoir un OVNI en train d’enlever une femme à l’aide de son faisceau lumineux.
Approchez-vous pour assister à la scène. L’OVNI disparaîtra en laissant la femme derrière lui. Parlez-lui et proposez votre aide, puis retournez vers sa voiture. Vous serez alors enlevé à votre tour par les extraterrestres. Après une transition, votre personnage se réveillera au même endroit, sans aucun souvenir de son enlèvement. Vous apprendrez également que trois jours se sont écoulés depuis votre disparition.
Cette première rencontre permet de débloquer le trophée ou succès « La vérité est ailleurs » . Mais ce n’est que le début de cette mystérieuse aventure.
Après votre enlèvement, il faudra patienter avant de pouvoir poursuivre la quête. Retournez à votre domicile et allez dormir. Le déclenchement de la prochaine séquence semble en partie aléatoire. Si rien ne se passe, continuez simplement d’autres activités pendant quelque temps, puis retournez vous coucher jusqu’à déclencher un rêve particulièrement étrange.
Vous vous réveillerez alors dans une immense pièce blanche qui semble appartenir à un vaisseau extraterrestre ou à un laboratoire. Plusieurs énigmes vous attendent pendant cette séquence. Retenez bien leurs solutions, car elles vous seront utiles pour la dernière étape de la quête.
Commencez par emprunter la porte menant à une pièce remplie d’étranges œufs extraterrestres. Pour traverser cette salle, restez accroupi et longez le mur de gauche en évitant de vous approcher des œufs. Ces derniers peuvent réagir à votre présence et éclater si vous vous en approchez trop. Si vous en déclenchez plusieurs, une immense tentacule finira par vous attraper et vous devrez recommencer la séquence.
Progressez donc lentement jusqu’à atteindre la sortie de l’autre côté de la pièce. Examiner les planètes pour trouver le laboratoire secret La salle suivante contient une représentation du système solaire. Approchez-vous de la sphère centrale et interagissez avec elle pour découvrir une étrange installation située quelque part dans Leonida.
Il s’agit en réalité d’un indice permettant de localiser le laboratoire secret que vous devrez visiter un peu plus tard. Une fois l’interaction terminée, une nouvelle porte s’ouvrira et vous pourrez poursuivre votre exploration.
Vous arriverez ensuite devant une porte équipée d’un digicode à quatre chiffres. Le code n’est pas nécessairement identique dans toutes les parties . Pour trouver la bonne combinaison, observez les barres lumineuses situées au-dessus du clavier. Chaque groupe de barres correspond à un chiffre. Il suffit de compter le nombre de barres dans chaque groupe, de gauche à droite, puis de saisir les quatre chiffres obtenus.
Par exemple, si vous distinguez successivement quatre, deux, un et trois barres, votre code sera 4213. D’autres combinaisons sont possibles, notamment 2143 ou 3214. Inutile donc de recopier systématique

articles.t: GTA 6 Could Actually Lose at Least 3 Game Awards Categories
articles.chapeau: Don't expect a Clair Obscur-style sweep
articles.txt:
After racking up an astonishing 99 rating on Metacritic — officially the highest ever — Grand Theft Auto 6 is more than the favorite to win Game of the Year at The Game Awards on Dec. 10. It's a certainty.
But this doesn't necessarily mean we're looking at an awards-night sweep of the kind Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 pulled off at the 2025 awards. There are one or two categories where GTA 6 may well lose, and it will need to win in every single one to match Clair Obscur 's record nine wins. ( GTA 6 has eight nominations, but that will surely go up to nine when the nominees for the fan-voted Players' Voice award are announced.)
This is also very likely a win for GTA 6 . It's rare for Best Game Direction not to go to the eventual GOTY winner. When it does happen, it's usually in years when there's no clear front-runner. That can be down to a weak field, as in 2021, when It Takes Two won Game of the Year and Deathloop won Best Direction, or an intensely competitive one like 2023, when Baldur's Gate 3 took GOTY and Alan Wake 2 won Game Direction. The gulf between GTA 6 and the rest of the field is so wide, I can't see another game winning Game Direction this time, even considering perennial awards darling (and two-time Game Direction winner) Remedy Entertainment has Control Resonant up in the same category this year.
Again, I think GTA 6 is ahead here, although it has strong competition from The Blood of Dawnwalker in particular. But Rockstar won Best Narrative for Red Dead Redemption 2 in 2018, and GTA 6 definitely shares that game's more mature storytelling style, while the majority of reviews highlighted how strongly the love story between Jason and Lucia anchors the game.
GTA 6 is an amazing-looking game, both technically and artistically, with acutely observed character looks and astounding environmental design. But The Game Awards tends not to reward outright realism in a contemporary setting in the Art Direction category. For example, in 2020, The Last of Us Part 2 was defeated by the more lush and painterly Ghost of Tsushima in this race.
Remedy is a two-time winner in this category, for Control and Alan Wake 2 ; the jury loves its combination of AAA sheen and striking, surreal visual design. It's the favorite, but I could see a win for The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time here too — as a dramatic and very successful reinterpretation of a classic, Nintendo's game certainly has the most noticeable art direction of the year.
Image: Nintendo EPD/Nintendo Will win: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time
This is a tight race. GTA 6 's soundtrack defies belief, but much of that rests on its vast library of licensed music, and there will be a perception (rightly or wrongly) that Rockstar flexed its massive buying power here rather than exercising thoughtful curation. More to the point, the Game Awards jury does not tend to reward licensed soundtracks in this category, preferring traditional, movie-style musical scores. (If there's a Final Fantasy game nominated, it's winning.)
So I think this award will rest mostly on Justice's score, and while the French electronic duo is a cool get for Rockstar, I'm not sure their moody synthwave can stand up to the timeless melodies of Koji Kondo in Nintendo's stunning new orchestrations. (Watch out for Ace Combat 8 sneaking up on the outside of this race, too.)
In the understanding of The Game Awards jury, more audio is better audio, so I think GTA 6 's teeming soundscape will win the day.
Angela Sant'Albano has been the favorite all year for her turn as Resident Evil: Requiem 's Grace, but Manni Perez is making a huge splash as Lucia. It's not quite a lock. This is one category where recency bias doesn't necessarily work in your favor; it's quite common for the Best Performance winner to feature in a game released earlier in the year, with a character players have spent more time with. Still, Lucia is undeniable.
In recent years, this category has reflected the opinions of Chinese gamers, who overwhelm the vote with a patriotic pick. Three of the last four Players' Voice winners have been Chinese games: Genshin Impact , Black Myth: Wukong , and Wuthering Waves . Phantom Blade Zero is arguably stronger than any of them.
I've got GTA 6 winning six of nine categories, which would put it joint third among all-time Game Awards winners, alongside Baldur's Gate 3 and God of War Ragnarӧk . ( The Last of Us Part 2 won seven awards.) Not too shabby. It would be a good result for The Game Award

Take-Two Interactive has previously attempted to identify the person or people behind the Cyberleek identity. Despite those efforts, the individual or group has continued making claims involving the unreleased game.
Cyberleek argues that the Xbox build could provide an opportunity for PC modders to run Grand Theft Auto VI through emulation. Although the game is available on Xbox, an official PC port has not been released.

articles.t: Leonida Brings GTA 6 PC Porting Tools to GitHub
articles.chapeau: The open-source Leonida project helps convert GTA 6 Xbox assets and shaders for PC, but the game cannot launch without a completed executable loader.
articles.txt:
203 Reads Last Update Nov 22, 2026 - 18:48 Share WhatsApp Smallest Font Largest Font PC developers have gained a new set of tools for working with the Xbox Series X version of Grand Theft Auto VI following the appearance of Leonida on GitHub on November 22, 2026. The open-source project aims to transform the console version into a native Windows application by translating system calls and graphics instructions into formats compatible with PC hardware.
According to the project's documentation, Leonida uses static recompilation to translate the console environment into a PC-compatible implementation. Its graphics conversion process transforms compiled RDNA2 programs into SPIR-V, allowing them to work through the Vulkan graphics API.
The project is distributed under the GPL-3.0 license. Its developers state that the repository does not include copyrighted game files, encryption keys, or executable modules.
Despite its progress, Leonida cannot currently launch Grand Theft Auto VI. The developers still need an executable file to complete the loader and the D3D12 graphics layer required for the Vulkan implementation.
However, the existing tools already demonstrate several working resource-conversion capabilities. According to the project information, Leonida can extract and convert all 26 game shaders into SPIR-V format.
The toolkit also supports exporting 3D models into OBJ files, textures into DDS format, and audio tracks into Ogg Opus or WAV files. These functions allow developers to examine and process different game assets without having a functioning PC version.
Building the project requires an unpacked Xbox Series X copy of Grand Theft Auto VI version 1.0.2.1 with readable files. The automated utilities locate the game installation and extract the necessary resources before generating shaders locally.
Windows 10 or Windows 11 in a 64-bit configuration is required for the main development environment. Users also need approximately 350 GB of available disk space to accommodate the working files.
The software requirements include Python 3.12 or later, .NET 8 SDK, Vulkan SDK, and LLVM 21 or later with AMD architecture support. Developers must also install Visual Studio 2022 with its C++ desktop components, Windows SDK version 10.0.26100 or later, and FFmpeg for audio conversion.
Linux users can also perform resource extraction and shader validation, according to the project documentation. The executable loader is intended to run through compatibility platforms such as Wine or Proton once the necessary components become available.
The project's development community has also expanded, with its GitHub repository attracting more than 8,200 stars and 147 contributors. Ongoing development includes improvements to graphics-command translation and support for emulating 64-thread shader groups on NVIDIA and Intel graphics cards.

Image: Rockstar Games/Decrypt Smallest Font Largest Font A leaked version of Grand Theft Auto 6 could reach PC users before Rockstar Games releases an official port, but a hacker known as Cyberleek is making the release of a crucial game file conditional on a cryptocurrency target. The developer of the leak has also promised to publish the file on November 23, 2026, regardless of whether the target is reached. According to PC Gamer, Cyberleek has distributed what it describes as a nearly complete 209 GB Xbox build of GTA 6 from November 2026 through a torrent.
However, the main executable remains unavailable, preventing modders from immediately attempting to run the game on PC. The executable is the missing component Cyberleek says could enable work on emulating the leaked Xbox version on PC. Its release is tied to the market capitalization of a cryptocurrency token called CYBERLEEK.
Cyberleek has set a $15 million market capitalization target for an early release. That figure represents half of the $30 million target previously proposed by the leaker in October.
As of the weekend, CYBERLEEK was trading at approximately $0.002, with a market capitalization of around $1.3 million. According to the reported figures, the token remained more than $13 million below the requested threshold. The token had also declined approximately 20% over the week. However, its limited liquidity means that market prices and capitalization figures could fluctuate substantially.
The arrangement has prompted concerns among cryptocurrency observers about the possibility of a speculative price increase followed by a rug pull, a practice in which token promoters abandon a project after attracting buyers. Cyberleek has separately claimed to possess a PlayStation 5 build that could serve as an alternative if the Xbox files prove unusable. Neither the claimed Xbox version nor the PlayStation 5 files have been independently verified as genuine.
The incident highlights the growing overlap between cryptocurrency speculation, game piracy, and artificial intelligence-assisted development. Modern Xbox game architecture is considered closer to conventional PC software than PlayStation architecture, potentially making certain emulation and porting efforts more accessible. AI coding tools have also accelerated decompilation work, contributing to a broader wave of AI-assisted game porting projects during 2026.
These developments have increased attention on the technical possibilities surrounding unofficial PC versions of console games. GTA 6 has also been associated with other cryptocurrency-related speculation. A trader previously made approximately $66,000 from a GTA 6-themed meme coin amid confusion surrounding cryptocurrency ticker symbols.
Separately, the game's digital-only, disc-free release has fueled debate about consumer rights. GameStop's CEO has argued that digital-only games have negatively affected consumers.
Rockstar Games has not announced an official PC version of Grand Theft Auto 6. The company could also pursue legal action against unauthorized distribution of its intellectual property, while Cyberleek's promised executable release remains scheduled for November 23, 2026.

articles.chapeau: GTA 6 PC port hopes rest on a 209GB Xbox leak with no executable. What Cyberleek claims, what is confirmed, and why a one-week port is doubtful.
articles.txt:
Image: Rockstar Games A group calling itself Cyberleek says it has put an alleged 209GB Xbox build of Grand Theft Auto VI online, and ARY News reports that the files have sparked hopes for a quick unofficial PC port . Technobezz carries the same story. The excitement is easy to understand, because PC players have no official version to wait for and no date to circle.
The catch is blunt. The package reportedly does not include the main executable file, so nobody can launch it as a game today. Rockstar Games has announced no PC version and no PC release date. Cyberleek says it will hand over the executable on November 23, 2026, which is tomorrow, and claims the game could be “emulated inside a week.” Every one of those claims remains unconfirmed. Our earlier piece on the 209 GB Xbox dump and the missing emulator covered the first hours of the story. This analysis goes further and asks what a quick PC port would actually demand.
We separate what outlets have confirmed from what the leak source merely says, explain why one missing file changes everything, compare the realistic routes to a PC version, and close with five predictions. Grand Theft Auto VI reportedly launched on consoles on November 19, 2026, so the stakes for Rockstar’s parent company, Take-Two Interactive, are high while the game is still in its first week of sales.

Add Shattered once in the Google app and our stories show up in your news suggestions.
The core claim is simple. Cyberleek says the files represent a November 2026 build of Grand Theft Auto VI, and that the build comes from an Xbox development environment. The reported size is 209GB. Several outlets, including PCMag, Rock Paper Shotgun and Neowin, ran stories on the release. PCMag described the leaker as returning and circulating an alleged Xbox build , which suggests the group has made leak claims before.
Reports also say the archive carries a package name, GTA6.Xbox.v1.0.2.1-CYBERLEEK. That label is itself unconfirmed. Anyone can name a folder, and a label tells you nothing about what the files do when you open them. Treat the name as a claim about the package, not as evidence of its contents.
Cyberleek describes the distribution as a torrent, and the group’s own wording says so directly. That matters for a practical reason. A torrent spreads quickly and cannot be recalled, so whatever the archive contains is now in many hands. It also means the files reach people who have no way to check them against a trusted original.
The cleanest summary is this. A group that PCMag says has returned with new leak claims says it has uploaded a large Xbox build. Outlets have reported that claim. None of the reports we reviewed describe an independent check of the dump, and none show a working executable. That is the ground floor of the story, and everything built on top of it is speculation.
News about leaks tends to blur two things: what outlets report and what anyone has verified. A report that a group made a claim is a fact. The claim itself is not. The table below sorts the main points of this story into those buckets, using only what the reports support.
Read down the middle column and a pattern appears. Almost nothing reaches the level of confirmed. The one firm item is the absence of an official PC announcement, and that is a statement about silence. Hopes for a quick port rest on claims from the very source that benefits from attention.
A game is more than its assets. Textures, audio, models and level data fill most of a 209GB package, but the executable is the program that ties them together. It holds the logic that loads a world, runs missions, simulates traffic and draws each frame. Without it, a pile of data files is just a very large archive.
That is why every report we reviewed stresses the gap. The files, as described, cannot launch. Nobody can hand a modder this archive today and watch a port appear. Cyberleek says it will release the missing piece, and that promise is the real hinge of the story. If the date passes with no executable, the hopes behind the headline collapse. If the file appears, a new and harder set of questions starts.

articles.t: GTA 6 PS5 and Xbox users protest after bans for sharing gameplay with nudity
articles.chapeau: Microsoft and Sony are cracking down on lewd GTA 6 gameplay captured by players. Xbox and PS5 gamers received suspensions for uploading clips featuring sunbathing or nude NPCs. Some critics think that sharing unedited footage from the approved Rockstar title should be safe.
articles.txt:
Rockstar 's new title carries a mature age rating for violence, strong language, and occasional nudity . Players are discovering the risks of sharing GTA 6 gameplay clips with adult-oriented content. An Xbox user received a 48-hour suspension for an upload depicting scantily-clad beachgoers . Meanwhile, a PS5 gamer suffered a longer punishment after taking a photo of a nudist colony.
By default, the Xbox Network automatically shares captured in-game footage with friends. Redditor sangobar documented how a beach clip triggered a flag, resulting in a two-day suspension. An email claimed that the media violated Community Standards or the Microsoft Services Agreement. Although the poster couldn't appeal, the ban didn’t prevent access to the single-player campaign .
Sangobar argues the video contained no nudity and the discipline was unjust. GTA 6 PS5 players are also finding the guidelines for promoting mature gameplay unclear. On social media, DerrickGott007 says he was given a one-month restriction on PSN social features . In this instance, NPCs wearing no clothing were the culprit.
Fans first learned the Leonida map included nudist colonies in a Cyberleek video from a development build. DerrickGott007 snapped an in-game photo in one of these locations before sending it to an acquaintance. The messaging system flagged the inappropriate imagery and responded accordingly.
It’s unclear if a Microsoft or Sony employee reviewed the footage, but both companies rely on AI-powered monitoring . Particularly with the beach example, a human may have recognized there was no infraction. A 2025 Digital Safety Content Report from Microsoft disclosed a high rate of successful appeals for false positives.
Some gamers believe it shouldn’t be their responsibility to filter out adult content. Xbox and PlayStation approved the GTA 6 release for their consoles, aware of its mature age rating. At worst, they should block the distribution of offensive media without penalizing a user.
Series X and S owners can reduce their chances of a ban by turning off automatic uploads. Until Sony comments, PS5 fans should be cautious about what GTA 6 gameplay they record and share on PSN messaging.

According to Leonida's description, since the Xbox Series X/S CPU is x86-64 like a PC, the "game's code is loaded and run[s} natively." The team behind the project, which includes assistance from Claude and roughly 75 other contributors, claims that the console's system software has also already been reimplemented.
Additionally, the Xbox Series X/S's "precompiled RDNA GPU programs are translated to SPIR-V for Vulkan" and the GTA 6 "models, textures, and audio" are all read directly from the disc image, which users need to provide from their own dumped copy of the Xbox version of GTA 6.
Like similar porting projects, Leonida doesn't feature GTA 6 's game files or keys. Right now, the game doesn't even boot on PC because the project is missing the game's executable, which Cyberleek's recent leak of the Xbox version doesn't include.
Credit: Rockstar Users on Reddit report that Cyberleek's Xbox build of GTA 6 features roughly 209GB of data. Screenshots of the leaked directory structure are also circulating online (check one out below). I haven't verified that the torrent is available (it's likely being shared through private trackers). Cyberleek says they'll release the missing executable file once a countdown expires, but that they'll drop it early if their shady cryptocurrency reaches $15 million in market capitalization (because, of course, a cryptocurrency scam is connected to this).
It's unclear how long it will take to get GTA 6 running on PC, but if the Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake is any indication, it could arrive sooner than expected. While GTA 6 is now available on the PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S, Rockstar hasn't announced a PC version. Rumors point to an official PC release arriving somewhere between six months and a year from now, similar to GTA V .
Hookshot was briefly pulled from GitHub after a dispute between NotRexed and the rest of the team behind the project. It's back on GitHub now, though. MagicBean's Longshot , a fork of Hookshot, continues the original project, with most of the team shifting over. In other GTA 6 -related news, with PS5 Remote Play or a capture card, plus apps like Veyra and a powerful gaming PC, several people have been able to run GTA 6 at 60fps and above with DLSS5 .

articles.txt:
Bluffton, OH From movies and tv to the lastest fashion trends and lifestyles. We are your one-stop for everything.
Remember Cyberleek? The Grand Theft Auto VI leaker with a meme coin and a dream claims to have dumped nearly the entire Xbox build of the game on launch day, and says the last missing piece is coming soon. It’s déjà vu, because we’ve been through this song and dance before.
On Oct. 10, Cyberleek tied a full build release to their coin’s market value hitting $30 million. The coin never came close and flamed out within days. This isn’t the first time it has crashed, either: Tom’s Hardware reported that the leaker cashed out roughly $250,000, mostly from accumulated trading fees, in late August, hours before Rockstar’s official gameplay reveal and just before the coin plunged.
That’s a bit like a magician announcing the big reveal and slipping out through the kitchen with the cash register. And what did we get in the meantime? Some Lucia clips picked by a fan poll and requested by basically nobody else, delivered with the energy of a guy who found a loophole in the “no refunds” policy.
Now the target has dropped to $15 million. Cyberleek says the final file is coming Monday, Nov. 23, no matter what, or sooner if the coin hits $15 million first. Half price, like a clearance rack at a Blockbuster that somehow survived into 2026 (OK, one of them did). Nothing says confidence like cutting your own ransom note in half and hoping nobody notices.
According to PC Gamer , Cyberleek says every file has been released except the main executable, from what the leaker calls the “full November 2026 build” of the game. Reports put the download at roughly 200 GB, with several outlets citing 209 GB. If that’s accurate, they’ve handed over the whole pantry and kept the oven. It’s like mailing someone every ingredient for a birthday cake, then standing outside their house holding the matches and asking for a tip.
One important caveat: as of this writing, nobody has confirmed the build is genuine. Everything about the build itself is Cyberleek’s claim. And files claiming to be Cyberleek builds have been linked to malware before, so this isn’t the torrent to get curious about.
Cyberleek’s pitch is that “this community will have it emulated inside a week, running far past 30fps.” Fine. Honestly, kind of compelling. I’ve watched grown adults argue about frame rates in a Walmart parking lot, so I understand the stakes. The catch: no working Xbox Series X emulator exists yet, according to Notebookcheck, so “inside a week” is doing a lot of heavy lifting.
GTA 6 has no official PC version, so Cyberleek is pitching emulation of the leaked console build as the way in. And if the Xbox build can’t be made to work, they say they’ll go after a PlayStation 5 build instead, a fallback they call “most likely never required.” Because apparently one console isn’t enough.
According to launch-day reports from PC Gamer and IGN, the meme coin was sitting at roughly $1.8 million to $1.9 million. Reaching $15 million in a few days would take an eightfold jump, the kind of growth you normally only see in a sourdough starter during lockdown, and even those eventually die in the back of the fridge. So the date is the trigger that actually matters: Monday, Nov. 23.
Maybe Cyberleek has the goods. Maybe they have a folder of loading screens and a very vivid imagination. Nobody knows, and my money’s on the second one, but if the build is real, Rockstar has a headache. Either way, we’ll find out soon. Grab some popcorn, and maybe a sturdy lawn chair.

In that time, Cyberleek dropped a manifesto (the " CYBERLEEK Edict ") championing consumer rights while simultaneously launching and cashing out on a meme coin (named $CYBERLEEK, of course) before disappearing into the void.

Zero, and the executable drops, no conditions. Unless the CYBERLEEK token reaches 15 million market cap first — then it drops immediately."

articles.t: GTA 6 PC : un pirate affirme pouvoir rendre le jeu jouable en une semaine grâce à une fuite Xbox
articles.chapeau: À peine sorti sur PS5 et Xbox, GTA 6 agite déjà la scène PC : le hacker Cyberleek promet un port jouable en une semaine grâce à une fuite Xbox. Entre build incomplète, memecoin et pression sur Rockstar, cette promesse intrigue autant qu’elle inquiète.
articles.txt:
À peine sorti sur PS5 et Xbox, GTA 6 agite déjà la scène PC : le hacker Cyberleek promet un port jouable en une semaine grâce à une fuite Xbox. Entre build incomplète, memecoin et pression sur Rockstar, cette promesse intrigue autant qu’elle inquiète.
Depuis la sortie de GTA 6 le 19 novembre 2026 sur PS5 et Xbox Series X|S, beaucoup se demandent encore quand la version PC arrivera. Un pirate qui se fait appeler Cyberleek promet d’abréger l’attente en rendant GTA 6 PC jouable en « moins d’une semaine » grâce à une fuite Xbox.
Dans un message du 19 novembre relayé par PC Gamer, le hacker affirme : « CL détient la build complète de novembre 2026 de Grand Theft Auto VI, et elle part en torrent, maintenant ». Il décrit une build de développement Xbox d’environ 209 Go et annonce un compte à rebours jusqu’au 23 novembre pour lâcher le fichier clé.
Selon les premiers retours de la scène sécurité comme VX‑Underground , les fichiers ressemblent à de vrais assets de Grand Theft Auto VI : textures, sons, scripts, données du moteur. Mais l’archive Xbox serait privée de son exécutable principal, le fameux .exe qui sert de chef d’orchestre. Sans lui, ces 209 Go restent un puzzle impossible à lancer.
C’est ce fichier que Cyberleek promet de publier, en expliquant qu’il s’agit « d’une build Xbox, pas d’une build PC » mais que « cette communauté l’aura émulée en moins d’une semaine, au‑delà de 30 fps ». Pour l’instant, rien ne prouve que l’exécutable soit réellement en sa possession.
Derrière la promesse de GTA 6 PC rapide se cache aussi un objectif financier. Le pirate lie la mise en ligne anticipée de l’exécutable au succès de son jeton crypto $CYBERLEEK : il réclame 15 millions de dollars, soit environ 14 millions d’euros de capitalisation, après un premier seuil à 30 millions de dollars, près de 28 millions d’euros, jamais atteint.
Sur le plan technique, cette promesse fait tiquer les spécialistes. Aucun émulateur Xbox Series X|S public ne sait aujourd’hui lancer un jeu aussi lourd que GTA 6 . Même avec le kit Xbox GDK , proche de Windows, il faudrait soit émuler tout l’environnement console, soit recompiler le code vers un exécutable PC, ce qui demande d’ordinaire des mois de travail.
Cette agitation attire déjà de faux sites « GTA 6 PC gratuit » et des launchers piégés par des malwares. Télécharger ces builds reste illégal en France, avec à la clé risques de poursuites et de vol de données.
Officiellement, Rockstar Games n’a toujours pas annoncé de version PC de Grand Theft Auto VI , même si des rumeurs évoquent un lancement début 2027 . L’ancien directeur technique Obbe Vermeij estime qu’un portage PC plus rapide serait dans l’intérêt du studio pour couper l’herbe sous le pied des ports sauvages dopés aux outils automatisés et des hackers comme Cyberleek .
En attendant une annonce officielle, la seule manière légale de profiter de GTA 6 sur un écran d’ordinateur reste le streaming de sa version PS5 ou Xbox via Remote Play ou Xbox Cloud Gaming. Entre menaces de leak, chantage au memecoin et protection juridique agressive de Rockstar, la promesse d’un GTA 6 PC jouable en une semaine tient plus du pari risqué que d’une feuille de route crédible.

articles.t: GTA 6 Leak Tied to $15 Million Crypto Goal as Pirated Build Spreads — BigGo Finance
articles.chapeau: An anonymous leaker known as Cyberleek has distributed a roughly 209 GB Xbox build of Grand Theft Auto 6 by torrent while withholding the main…
articles.txt:
Add preferred source An anonymous leaker known as Cyberleek has distributed a roughly 209 GB Xbox build of Grand Theft Auto 6 by torrent while withholding the main executable needed to attempt a PC port. The file is promised for Nov. 23, but would be released early if the CYBERLEEK meme coin reaches a $15 million market cap - down from an earlier $30 million target. The token was trading near $0.002 at a value of about $1.3 million, far short of the goal, and has drawn accusations of a pump-and-dump scheme. None of the files has been verified, Rockstar has announced no PC version, and security researchers report thousands of malware detections tied to fake GTA 6 downloads. Key Elements Cyberleek GTA 6 Rockstar Games CYBERLEEK token Grand Theft Auto PC Gamer Kaspersky GameStop PlayStation 5 Xbox A figure using the handle Cyberleek has posted what is described as a roughly 209 GB Xbox build of Grand Theft Auto 6 to torrent networks, but is holding back the one file that matters most to anyone hoping to run the game on a computer: the main executable.
According to PC Gamer, the leaker has attached a financial condition to that final piece. Cyberleek says the executable will be published on Nov. 23 either way, but will be released early if the CYBERLEEK meme coin reaches a $15 million market capitalization - half the $30 million threshold floated in October.
The market has not cooperated. The token was changing hands near $0.002 over the weekend, putting its value at roughly $1.3 million, or more than $13 million below the stated trigger. It has shed about 20% over the past week, though pricing on a micro-cap asset with very little liquidity can swing violently in either direction.
The missing executable is the piece that would allow modders to begin the work of recompilation - adapting console code so it runs on PC hardware - potentially delivering a playable version long before Rockstar Games plans to sell one. The leaker has said the process could take about a week once the file is available, and has also claimed to hold a PlayStation 5 build as a fallback should the Xbox files prove unusable.
None of the leaked material has been independently verified as authentic, and Rockstar has announced no PC version of the game. The publisher, which has a long record of litigating against leaks and cheats, could pursue legal action rather than tolerate a port.
Skepticism has been loud. Critics have described the arrangement as a shakedown or, worse, an attempt to inflate the coin ahead of a rug pull - the crypto maneuver in which a token's backers abandon it after attracting buyers.
Note: Market figures reflect thin trading in a small-cap token and can change sharply.
The episode lands at the intersection of three trends that have been converging all year: crypto speculation, game piracy and AI-assisted coding. Modern Xbox titles are architecturally closer to PC software than PlayStation releases, which shortens the path to a workable port, and AI programming tools have sped up the decompilation work that such conversions require.
It also extends a turbulent launch window for Grand Theft Auto 6. Crypto traders have repeatedly tried to profit from the game's release, including one who captured about $66,000 amid confusion over ticker symbols. The title's digital-only, disc-free format has separately drawn criticism, with GameStop's chief executive arguing that all-digital games have hurt consumers.
The leak has arrived alongside a wave of fraudulent downloads. Security firm Kaspersky has logged 27,416 detections of GTA 6-related malware and unwanted software since June, according to ZDNET, with fake PC versions ranging from crude AI-generated clones to files designed to hijack machines for crypto mining or to steal personal data. The only official release remains the PlayStation 5 edition; PC players can currently stream it through Sony's Remote Play app.
Rockstar's habit of staggering platforms is central to the frustration driving interest in the leak. Red Dead Redemption 2 reached PC about a year after consoles, and Grand Theft Auto 5 took nearly two years.
For the industry, the stakes go beyond one title. If major new releases can be played free on other platforms within days of launch, publishers lose revenue that funds subsequent development - a threat that falls hardest on smaller studios. The likely defensive response would be tighter always-online requirements, which tend to inconvenience paying customers most.

articles.chapeau: CyberLeek says it leaked a GTA VI Xbox development build but holds back the executable. See what is confirmed, what is not, and what comes next.
articles.txt:
Image: Rockstar Games A hacker persona called CyberLeek says it has put a Grand Theft Auto VI development build on the internet, and the first reports landed within a day of the game’s launch. Eurogamer reported that the group claims to have leaked a full development build, while IGN and others stressed that one crucial file is missing. That file is the main executable, which means the files on offer cannot launch the game. Nobody has shown that the archive is real.
This analysis separates what is on the record from what is marketing. The CyberLeek GTA VI leak rests on a short statement, a torrent listing and a countdown. Our earlier report on the 209 GB Xbox dump covered the size and the emulator problem. This piece goes wider: the claims one by one, the money angle, the risks for players and what could happen before November 23.

Add Shattered once in the Google app and our stories show up in your news suggestions.
The core claim is simple. CyberLeek says it holds a November 2026 build of Grand Theft Auto VI and that it is distributing the files by torrent. Reports describe the build as an Xbox development build, not a PC build. The torrent listing reportedly carries the title “XBOX BUILD 1.0.2.1 (NOV 2026)”, according to the coverage we reviewed.
The group did not publish everything. Reports from Malay Mail and IGN say the main executable is held back. In the group’s telling, that single file stays locked behind a countdown. Reporters have not seen any proof that the rest of the archive is complete, and that gap defines the whole story.
The timing also matters. The leak claim surfaced after GTA VI went on sale, which gave the group the largest audience it could ask for. Outlets including mxdwn Games, Nacionale, IGN, Wolf’s Gaming Blog, Eurogamer and Notebookcheck all ran versions of the story. Every one of them frames it as an allegation, and none reports a confirmation from Rockstar Games.
Related guides: From the same topic area, our evergreen pick is PS5 Pro vs Xbox Series X , a page we keep current rather than a story that dates; the Shattered guides hub groups it with the other setup guides and comparisons we maintain, each listed with a one-line description written for it.
Most headlines blur three different things: what the group said, what outlets observed and what anyone has verified. Separating them is the only way to read this story honestly. The table below lists the five claims that carry the narrative and marks each by the evidence behind it.
Look at the pattern. The things that are confirmed are things the group said about itself. The things a reader would care about, such as whether the files are genuine and complete, remain open. That is a thin foundation for a story that dominated gaming headlines for a day.
The statement is the only primary document in this story, so it deserves a close read. Rock Paper Shotgun published the text, and its report quotes the group saying: “CL holds the full November 2026 build of Grand Theft Auto VI, and it is going out by torrent.” The same statement adds the group’s own terms: “Honest terms, as always: it is an Xbox build this time, not a PC build.”
The statement then turns to the community. Per Rock Paper Shotgun, CyberLeek wrote: “This community will have it emulated inside a week, running far past 30fps.” That is a forecast, not a fact, and it carries real weight in how the story spreads. It tells readers the files are useful and that someone else will do the hard work of making them run.
The closing line is a marketing slogan. Rock Paper Shotgun reports the group ending with: “CL told you not to preorder for a reason. articles.txt:
CyberLeek has reportedly uploaded more than 200 GB of GTA VI XBOX game files online, but there is still one important file missing from the release: the main executable.
The files first appeared online on November 19, shortly after GTA VI’s launch. The package reportedly contains a large portion of the game’s Xbox development files, but without the executable, users cannot properly access or run the game.
According to Rockstar Games community researcher Lucas7yoshi , the uploaded files are indeed from an XBOX build of GTA VI. However, he pointed out that this is an older version of the game, as it does not even include the separate censorship version for Australia and New Zealand.
More importantly, the game’s assets are encrypted with a key obtained from the main executable. This means that simply downloading the files is not enough to access their contents.
CyberLeek initially announced that the missing executable would be released on November 23, regardless of whether its cryptocurrency reached a certain market value.
However, the group also introduced a condition that could make the release happen earlier. The original target was a $15 million market cap for its CYBERLEEK token. This requirement has since reportedly been lowered to $6 million.
According to GTA community member PLTytus , the token currently has a market cap of around $1.44 million. He also reminded followers that CyberLeek had promised to release the executable once its poll ends on Monday at 6 PM CET, even if the market cap target is not reached.
This means November 23 could be an important date for anyone following the situation, although there is still no independent confirmation that the missing file will actually be released as promised.
One of CyberLeek’s biggest claims is that the community could get the XBOX build running on PC within a week, potentially achieving performance above 30 FPS. However, this is far from guaranteed.
The uploaded files are from an XBOX version of GTA VI, not a native PC build. Even if the missing executable becomes available, getting the game running on PC would require additional work from developers and the emulation community.
For now, there is no confirmed playable PC version coming from this leak, and Rockstar Games has not announced a PC release date. It is also worth remembering that the authenticity and completeness of the entire package have not been independently established.
We will have to wait and see whether CyberLeek actually releases the missing executable on November 23 and what the community manages to do with the files afterward. articles.t: GTA 6: PC gamers welcome unofficial PC port despite potential damage to the industry
articles.chapeau: GTA 6 is finally here, but PC gamers are still waiting – at least for an official release. An unofficial PC version could already be on the way. Despite the potential damage such recompilations could do to the gaming industry, the prospect has been met with largely positive reactions online.
articles.txt:
On the day GTA 6 launched, hacker Cyberleek released large portions of the Xbox version , potentially paving the way for an unofficial PC port. The process in question is known as recompilation, which involves adapting a game's code to run on another platform. Cyberleek believes modders could get the game running on PC within a week. On Reddit , the otherwise controversial hacker is receiving plenty of support – despite the potential harm such releases could cause to game developers.
PC gamers are clearly frustrated about having to wait for GTA 6 . However, the enthusiasm surrounding the prospect of an unofficial PC version arriving so soon appears to be driven largely by resentment toward Rockstar's long-standing strategy of releasing its games on consoles first and PC later. Many users accuse Rockstar of deliberately encouraging players to buy the same game twice. Those eager to play GTA 6 at launch may purchase the console version, only to buy it again on PC later to enjoy improved graphics. Some commenters have even openly stated that they intend to play the unofficial port. Others hope that rapid progress on the recompilation will put pressure on Rockstar to bring forward the official PC release.
Whether the unofficial port will actually be playable next week remains uncertain. Modders are still missing a crucial file: the game's executable (EXE), without which it cannot be launched. Cyberleek says he plans to release it on November 23, but whether that will be enough to produce a working PC version so quickly remains to be seen. There are also broader concerns about the potential consequences of such recompilations. If newly released games become available for free on other platforms shortly after launch, developers could lose valuable revenue. For smaller studios in particular, those losses could threaten their survival. Over time, this could make it harder to finance new games and encourage publishers to introduce stricter always-online requirements – ultimately leaving players worse off as well.

articles.t: GTA 6 Quietly Mocks an Infamous Donald Trump Florida Moment
articles.chapeau: Rockstar said it wouldn't directly satirize Trump — but GTA 6 takes a shot anyway
articles.txt:
Grand Theft Auto 6 takes place in Rockstar Games' fictional version of Florida, so many wondered how the game might tackle President Donald Trump, who spends much of his time at his private club, Mar-a-Lago. Prior to release, Rockstar dispelled any notion that the game might directly address the current President of the United States. Doing so might make the game feel dated, according to Rockstar North studio head Rob Nelson. Now that the game is out, fans have discovered that GTA 6 does quietly acknowledge Trump.
The Easter egg probably isn't what you're expecting, and it doesn't really mention the Republican President's controversial politics. The shout-out does, however, poke fun at Trump's infamy for allegedly skipping out on the bill. You may have already seen it without realizing what it is. The story is a hyper-localized one involving a 2023 Trump visit to Miami's iconic Cuban restaurant, Versailles.
According to the Miami New Times , Trump came to the restaurant after being arraigned at a Miami courthouse over allegations of retaining government secrets and conspiring to obstruct justice. When he arrived at the restaurant, there was a crowd — and they were so ecstatic to see him that they began singing "Happy Birthday" to him. His birthday was technically the next day, and the man had just been indicted on 37 federal charges , but it didn't matter. The fans evidently wanted to express their love for the politician/reality TV show host in some way.
Trump gladly lapped up the attention and responded by declaring there would be "food for everyone!" The crowd cheered: They thought Trump was implying he was going to pick up their tab.
You're never going to believe this , but Trump did not, in fact, purchase anything for anyone. The Miami New Times reported that the President only stuck around for about 10 minutes before leaving. Since the incident, there's been some debate over whether Trump truly slighted anyone during the visit . He wasn't there for long, so could anyone truly have expected him to pull out his wallet?
However you interpret it, GTA 6 hides a reference to this controversial Florida moment through a small detail in its digital recreation of Versailles. The video game version of the establishment is called Antoinette, but the restaurant's reputation as a Miami staple and the building's matching exteriors heavily imply that Antoinette is based on a real-world restaurant. Even the restaurant's proprietors have made this connection.
TikToker Quique took a closer look at the GTA 6 version of the locale and found that there's a flier hanging from one of the windows. It reads: "All government officials must pay before leaving. Thank you." The connection between the real-life incident and GTA 6 's joke seems clear, according to fans from Florida in the TikTok video's comments.
Image: Quique/Tiktok It's a funny reference that reflects Rockstar's dedication to capturing Florida , and Miami in particular, to the fullest possible extent. As far as things go, though, it's a fairly tame Donald Trump moment that won't ruffle many political feathers. For a series known for lampooning American politics, that's kind of disappointing. You can't really extricate Trump from Florida, after all.
Anyway, my favorite part of the whole story is the interviews the Miami New Times conducted with the people who serenaded Trump​​​​​​​ at the restaurant after the President left the premises.
"He's the only one that will fight for us, for you, for me, for the people watching this at home," he said of the encounter, in which the president had arguably failed to keep his promise to the public just minutes earlier.

Le groupe de hackers Cyberleak affirme distribuer en torrent une build Xbox complète de Grand Theft Auto VI datant de novembre 2026 et prétend que les joueurs PC pourraient avoir le jeu « émulé en une semaine ». , une promesse qui se heurte de plein front à un mur technique : aucun émulateur Xbox Series X|S fonctionnel n'existe.
Cyberleak a déclaré dans un message du 19 novembre détenir la build Xbox complète et que les fichiers étaient diffusés immédiatement en torrent. Les premiers coups d'œil jetés sur la version par des membres de la communauté des hackers suggèrent qu'elle est authentique mais qu'il manque le fichier .EXE du lanceur nécessaire pour la faire tourner, et Cyberleak affirme que cet exécutable est « verrouillé derrière un compte à rebours » jusqu'au 23 novembre sauf si son jeton crypto atteint d'abord une capitalisation de 15 millions de dollars .
L'archive de logiciels malveillants vx-underground, qui a inspecté le torrent, affirme que les fichiers contiennent de véritables éléments de GTA 6 et que des gens pourraient y jouer sur PC dès lundi si le .exe sort le 23 comme promis.
> wake up > take a shit > get out of bed > check beep boop > over 9000 DMs > "SCHMEELI, GTA VI LEAK" > ??? > sends link > torrent > ok > look inside > actual assets > huh > squint eyes > look closer > not larp huh, how about that. the cyberleek guy released the full xbox gta 6… pic.twitter.com/1MDrGI97Dy
Le calendrier d'une semaine est l'affirmation de Cyberleak elle-même, et elle mérite du scepticisme pour deux raisons. D'abord, le groupe a un historique documenté d'utilisation de fuites précédentes de GTA 6 pour faire monter un programme de cryptomonnaie de 250 000 dollars, donc ses dates annoncées sont mieux traitées comme des affirmations que comme des événements programmés.
Ensuite, et plus fondamentalement, l'émulation est peut-être le mauvais mot pour ce qui suivrait la sortie d'un exécutable. Aucun émulateur Xbox Series X|S fonctionnel n'existe encore, il n'y a donc pas de route toute prête d'une build Xbox extraite vers une version PC jouable. Un portage non officiel fonctionnel dépendrait plutôt d'une recompilation, convertissant le code de la console pour tourner nativement sur PC, un chemin bien plus lent et moins certain que les taux d'images par seconde dont se targue Cyberleak.
GTA 6 est sorti sur console le 19 novembre, et Rockstar n'a annoncé aucune version PC. Des rumeurs évoquent un portage officiel début 2027, et l'ancien directeur technique de Rockstar, Obbe Vermeij, a soutenu que le studio bénéficierait à sortir un portage PC tôt, compte tenu de l'essor des portages assistés par IA. Cyberleak, dont le nom apparaît sous la forme « Cyberleek » dans certains titres repris par la presse, indique que si la version Xbox ne débouche pas sur un portage PC, il se tournerait plutôt vers une version PS5.
Rockstar n'a fait aucune déclaration sur la fuite. Cyberleak affirme que l'exécutable Xbox suivra le 23 novembre, quel que soit le résultat du programme de cryptomonnaie.

articles.t: GTA 6 PC Port Leak: 209 GB Xbox Dump, No Emulator
articles.chapeau: GTA 6 PC port leak: Cyberleek 209 GB Xbox dump lacks its executable, and no Xbox Series X|S emulator exists. What is verified and what is not.
articles.txt:
Image: Rockstar Games The GTA 6 PC port leak story took a sharper turn on November 21, 2026, two days after the console launch. A leaker calling itself Cyberleek says it put a roughly 209 GB Xbox build of Grand Theft Auto VI into circulation, and XDA Developers reported the claim as an unverified release of a dumped build. Nobody has confirmed the files are real. The reported dump also lacks the main executable, so the game cannot start.
That gap is the whole story. Cyberleek says the community will turn an Xbox build into a PC game within a week, yet reports describe no working Xbox Series X|S emulator that could run it. Our earlier report on the dump covered what appeared on the leaker’s site. This analysis asks a different question: how far is a 209 GB Xbox archive from a playable Windows version, and what do the headlines get right and wrong?
We tie every claim below to a named outlet, and we separate what the reports state from what only the leaker asserts. Rockstar Games has not officially announced a PC port, according to the coverage we reviewed. Everything about a PC route to the game remains speculation for now.

Cyberleek claims to hold a November 2026 build of Grand Theft Auto VI and says it is distributing the archive by torrent. PCMag reported the claim on November 20 and described a download of about 209 GB that the group says contains a decrypted Xbox build. VGTimes added that a link on the group’s site carried a label reading XBOX BUILD 1.0.2.1 (NOV 2026), and that journalists had seen the site itself.
The timing matters. Reports place the post on November 19, the same day the game reached PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S. A leak that lands on launch day maximizes attention, and that pattern fits a group that has spent months building an audience around Rockstar’s biggest release.
PCMag also reported that the archive appeared to include files tied to Rockstar’s RAGE engine and Xbox files connected with AMD graphics technology. That detail suggests the listing looks like a real console package, though a convincing file tree proves little by itself. File listings and screenshots are easy to stage, and a name on a folder is not a working game.
Cyberleek also drew a line between this release and a PC release. Its own wording, as quoted by GamesRadar, admitted that this is an Xbox build and not a PC build. We come back to that admission below, because it changes how readers should weigh the PC port framing that dominates search results.
Most of what circulates today is a claim about a claim. Outlets such as PCMag, GameSpot, IGN and Gamereactor UK report that Cyberleek says things, and several note that they could not check the files. The table sorts the main points by how well the coverage supports them.
The pattern is clear. Only two things hold up across outlets: a leaker made public claims, and the reported package cannot launch without a file the leaker withholds. Authenticity sits at the bottom of the confidence scale. The Ma-no.org write-up said Eurogamer could not confirm that the advertised files exist, and The GTA 6 Map reached a similar conclusion in its own coverage.
An executable is the program that loads everything else. Game data, models, audio and scripts sit in archives, and the executable decides how to read them and when to run them. Without it, the 209 GB of reported content is a very large pile of assets with no way to start.
GameSpot reported that the absent executable prevents the build from launching as a playable game. Cyberleek itself describes holding that single file back on a countdown. The group’s framing is that every other file is out and only the launcher is held, a tactic that keeps attention on the story for days.
Assets alone can still interest people. Modelers, datamining communities and analysts can inspect meshes, textures, map files and configuration data if the files are real and readable. That kind of material feeds speculation videos and wiki pages. It does not produce a running game.
A console executable also differs from a Windows one at the instruction and system level. An Xbox title targets a fixed hardware platform and a specific operating environment.
